<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>キャストアウェイ</b> &nbsp;·&nbsp; ずっと、昼。 &nbsp;·&nbsp; <i>daytime, all the way through</i><br>
  <sub>Short Shadow Records SSR-1992 &nbsp;·&nbsp; one island, one palm, ten hours &nbsp;·&nbsp; side B is also noon</sub>
</p>

**Castaway** (working title) is a ten-hour lo-fi video for YouTube, and this is its sleeve. A young woman sits alone on a very small island with one tall palm and a raft, nodding to the music on her headphones. Every so often, something happens. A message in a bottle washes straight back to her feet. A drone lowers a parcel, and the parcel is more headphones. A shark surfaces in headphones of its own and nods along. Then she goes back to nodding, and it is still daytime, because it is always daytime: the video has no night in it, by design.

It is an unofficial remake inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of *Johnny Castaway*, the 1992 desert-island screensaver, repainted as a sunny, hand-painted coastal scene: 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps. More than 90 activities take their turn, most of them on four timers and the rest as follow-ups. Every one starts on the next bar of the music, and every sound is synthesized from code.

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

<details>
<summary><b>Side A, Side B</b>: the full running order, and how a side gets played</summary>

```text
  SHORT SHADOW RECORDS · SSR-1992 · CASTAWAY · 10:00:00 · SEED 1992

  SIDE A · NOON ........................... one track every 2 to 5 min
    A1  Coconut, Eyes Closed ................................ 0:27-0:51
    A2  Nibbles, Nothing (fishing) .......................... 0:55-2:17
    A3  Sandcastle (Tide Version) ........................... 0:57-1:54
    A4  Jogging Laps ........................................ 0:21-0:38
    A5  A Slow Lap to the Waterline, and Back ............... 0:22-0:42

  SIDE B · STILL NOON
   every 12 to 25 min
    B1  Return to Sender (a message in a bottle) ............ 1:17-2:17
    B2  A Turtle Drops By ................................... 3:13-6:06
    B3  Coconut Meets Crab (crab keeps coconut) ............. 1:11-2:42
    B4  Kumara, Planted ..................................... 0:25-0:44
   every 30 to 60 min
    B5  More Headphones, by Drone ........................... 0:39-0:57
    B6  One Bar, Top of the Palm ............................ 1:54-4:10
    B7  The Cat on the Crate .............................. 11:04-26:46
    B8  Shark in Headphones (On the Beat) ................... 0:49-1:17
    B9  Selfies from the Tour Boat .......................... 0:52-1:21
    B10 Shaka (Hydrofoil Version) ........................... 0:30-0:51
    B11 Fire by Friction .................................... 0:43-1:11
    B12 Hammock ............................................. 1:35-3:59
    B13 Lookout, Top of the Palm ............................ 0:47-1:15
    B14 Spear Fishing ....................................... 0:39-1:07
   every 3 to 6 hours
    B15 She Could Leave Any Time ............................ 1:19-1:59

  HIDDEN TRACKS (they only play after something else)
    The Tide Takes It ........... 5 to 30 min after any sandcastle
    The Reply ................... 1 to 3 hours after a bottle comes back
    Kumara, Leafy ............... 1.5 to 2.5 hours after the planting
    Kumara, in Flower ........... 2 to 3 hours after that
```

A selection, not the whole pressing: [activities.toml](activities.toml) held 94 activities when checked on 2026-10-02 (81 on the four timers, 13 chained follow-ups), and more arrive every few hours. Times are each routine's shortest and longest run; the sleeve prints the middle of the range. When a timer goes off it picks one activity from its side, by weight, among the ones free to run right now, so in a typical 10-hour run (the median of 200 simulated runs, as the file's header says) side A plays about 155 times, the 12-to-25-minute timer about 30, the 30-to-60-minute timer about 13 and the rarest about twice, plus the hidden tracks. She is busy about a third of the time. The rest is the long instrumental: her, nodding.

Lanes let tracks overlap, so a visitor can drift past while she is busy with a coconut, and every activity waits for the next bar of the music (one every 3 seconds) so every punchline lands on the beat. `python tools/schedule.py` checks the file and simulates a 10-hour run. The default run is 10:00:00 with seed 1992, which is also the catalogue number.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Liner notes</b>: the sound, made entirely from code</summary>

<br>

Every sound in Castaway is synthesized by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no stock loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies. More than 150 sound files so far, and growing.

- **The theme**: a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major, a ii-V-I-vi progression over 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds, played by electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums and vinyl crackle. The crackle is synthesized too. This sleeve has never been near a needle.
- **The ocean**: its own seamless 60-second loop, under everything.
- **Mastering**: the mix sits at -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP, and levels can be set for the master and for each routine.
- **Reviews**: none yet. Nobody has listened to it. The sleeve is ready before the record, which is how a lot of records go.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Pressing notes</b>: how the record is cut</summary>

<br>

The renderer is a web page with a live preview. Run `python tools/serve.py`, open http://127.0.0.1:8765/, and it exports a frame-exact, YouTube-ready MP4: the browser encodes the picture as H.264 with WebCodecs (68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p30 in Chrome), then the server mixes the sound and joins the two. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages. The page itself is [web/index.html](web/index.html).

`python tools/render_demo.py --dev` renders a dev reel of every activity with a heads-up display, using the older Python reference renderer. Hard cuts and stepped movement are the house style for motion: the needle drops, it does not glide. The label on the record gives its tempo, 80 BPM, in the place where a real label gives its speed.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>The obi, translated</b></summary>

<br>

| On the strip | Reads | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| キャストアウェイ | kyasuto-awei | Castaway, in katakana |
| ずっと、昼。 | zutto, hiru | Daytime, all the way through. (A project rule: no night scenes.) |
| 定価 10:00:00 | teika | List price: ten hours, payable in time |
| SSR-1992 | | Catalogue number, after the default seed |

Short Shadow Records is invented, and named for noon, when shadows are shortest. The sleeve is an original drawing in the manner of early-1980s Japanese city pop LP art: no painting was traced and no real label, artist or sleeve is being imitated.

</details>

<p align="center"><sub>Unofficial: inspired by <i>Johnny Castaway</i> (1992), and not affiliated with it or its owners. Side B is also noon.</sub></p>
